components.name: Source disclosure
components.html:
Full protocol: host, runtimes, guards and completion
Host and date
7 November 2026, 07:42–07:43 UTC. Apple M1 Max, 10 logical CPUs, 64 GiB RAM; arm64 MacBookPro18,4. macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Darwin 25.6.0.
Sampling order
Three fresh process pairs, all serial: official/native, native/official, official/native. No process reuse, profiler, forced garbage collection or discarded warmups. Filesystem and operating-system caches were not flushed.
Timed operation
Official: load/parse/expand + check. Native: parse + expand + check, including eager parser-fuel setup. Startup, emission and external C compilation are excluded. The ratio divides the two source-processing medians, not individual phase medians or old timing receipts.
Official runtime
Node 23.11.0, V8 12.9.202.28-node.14; --experimental-strip-types --max-old-space-size=6144 --max-semi-space-size=128. Worker limits: 6,144 MiB old generation, 128 MiB young generation and 256 MiB stack. Node may use helper threads.
Native runtime
Cached diagnostic -O1 split-LLVM executable; one compute thread, GPU off (+RTS --threads 1 --gpu off --RTS). Each sample recorded 17 eager parser-fuel rows of 8,000,000 cells and ordered parse, expansion and checking phases.
Memory and guards
Bun 1.4.3 launches the shared guardian. It samples the owned compiler-command process tree every 10 ms: Node main process and worker for official, native process for self-hosted. Bun launcher, guardian and cohort parent are excluded for both. RSS and physical-footprint stop guards are each 8,192 MiB, with a 600-second timeout and 1-second termination grace. These are sampled guards, not hard allocation quotas or exact allocation peaks.
Completion checks
All six samples completed with their guards satisfied. Official runs covered the 52-file input map, 2,420 definition bodies and 2,954 validation events, with no holes or unchecked bodies. Native runs returned CheckSuccess for all 17 modules. No checks were excluded and no outputs were patched. The 35 foreign JavaScript files belong to the retained closure; no JavaScript emission or execution is timed.
Input identity
Source files, compiler/runtime artifacts, manifests, receipts and protocol helpers were rehashed before and after every sample and after the cohort. Hashing used bounded 64 KiB buffers in the unmeasured parent. The selected closure’s sorted source-tuple SHA-256 is 2555918b9caf261ab6a85fad8ef8fb132a87d9c835b77ee3a86cdefaed1dca01.
Whole-command time
Separately, guardian elapsed-time medians were 3.082 s official (2.551–3.660 s range) and 28.154 s native (25.960–34.264 s). These include startup, source processing and teardown; they are not the headline timing boundary.

narrative.overview:
The system is an artifact-led engineering report: cool off-white paper, green-black ink, hairline rules, real source code, and diagrams that expose boundaries and ownership. The heading names the subject rather than making a slogan. A compiled program, not a promotional metric, shares the opening with the introduction.

Archivo carries prose and interface labels. Fragment Mono is reserved for source, emitted code, checksums, actual execution results, and numerical data. Code regions and diagram nodes use square rules to describe real artifacts or conceptual structure; they are not decorative content cards.

Motion only acknowledges interaction: architecture nodes change fill and border over 180ms. Reduced motion removes transitions and smooth scrolling. Rules and spacing carry hierarchy; there are no shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Literal headings with a 52px desktop title cap and natural wrapping.
Open ruled sections, square controls, and no decorative containers.
Archivo for reading; Fragment Mono for code and measured values.
One visible comparison table with explicit units, sample ranges, and measurement scope.
Keyboard-visible focus and progressive enhancement of the architecture trace.
A recomposed mobile reading column, with wide data isolated in a scrollable region.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Yellow highlights evidence or selection; it does not mean faster, accepted, or correct. Keep the result and its scope explicit in words.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Archivo carries prose and interface labels. Fragment Mono carries code, identifiers, checksums, and measured table values; do not set prose paragraphs in it.

rules.name: The Literal Title Rule
rules.body: Name the subject directly. Keep the implemented title scale and natural wrapping; do not reintroduce an oversized slogan or forced display lines.

rules.name: The Reading Column Rule
rules.body: Recompose content for mobile instead of shrinking the desktop page. Keep prose readable and contain wide data in its own scroll region.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Separate with a rule, a fill, or spacing. Focus is a 2px ink outline at 5px offset, never a glow.

rules.name: The Square-End Rule
rules.body: Keep square edges. Do not introduce pills, rounded cards, circular icon buttons, or decorative enclosures.

dos: Do use literal headings and preserve the modest title scale and natural wrapping.
Do distinguish architecture, comparable measurements, and historical validation with explicit scope.
Do keep running prose at 17px/1.65 and a 68ch measure.
Do keep cross-implementation measurements together in one table, and distinguish a single-run phase decomposition from that comparison.
Do use yellow only for evidence, selection, and interaction emphasis—not as a favorable verdict.
Do retain visible keyboard focus and progressive enhancement.
Do contain wide tables in labelled, focusable scroll regions.
donts: Don't introduce slogans, forced display lines, or a giant promotional hero.
Don't require internal experiment or generation names to understand the report.
Don't add cards, shadows, gradients, blur, texture, or rounding.
Don't treat lower memory or successful validation as evidence of faster compilation.
Don't bring back runtime tabs, animated comparison bars, or status badges that no longer exist.
Don't set prose paragraphs in Fragment Mono or hide the primary results behind JavaScript.
